phylogenetic_basis: Bohs et al. 2007 Acta Horticulturae 745 DOI 10.17660/ActaHortic.2007.745.8; Stern et al. 2010 Systematic Botany DOI 10.1600/036364410X539934
notes: Section Crinitum is sister to section Androceras and includes S. lycocarpum; Crinitum representatives are actinomorphic and isantherous. S. lycocarpum has independent bee/buzz-pollination evidence. S. lycocarpum was adjudicated under the frozen SOURCE_QUALITY tie-break after consideration of equivalent close-section candidates; no BALANCE predictor value was used in selection.

phylogenetic_basis: Jiang et al. 2021 Journal of Systematics and Evolution DOI 10.1111/jse.12744; M. australasica is sister to the rest of Monochoria while M. korsakowii is the second split; BALANCE 68-shared-single-copy-CDS plastome audit ranks M. australasica closer than M. cyanea on the registered common-site p-distance surface; diagnostic is plastid-only
notes: M. australasica is source-resolved as nonheterantherous/non-reciprocal enantiostylous. The registered high-resolution plastome diagnostic closes the closest-control candidate ranking against M. cyanea under the frozen phylogenetic-distance tie-break. Direct species-level effective animal-pollination eligibility remains unresolved; Leijs et al. 2020 reports Amegilla territorial behaviour above water rather than a source-secure flower-visitation/pollination event. Selection therefore remains SCREENED rather than ADJUDICATED.

phylogenetic_basis: S. alata belongs to clade II. Every sampled clade-II candidate audited in the frozen search fails the heteranthery-absence gate. The next eligible grain is clade III, containing both S. atomaria and S. spectabilis. S. spectabilis has source-secure homomorphic fertile stamens and direct effective animal-pollination evidence; S. atomaria has the same clade-level grain but weaker pollination evidence, so the preregistered SOURCE_QUALITY tie-break selects S. spectabilis.
notes: Replacement control selected only after the sampled clade-II negative-control search was exhausted. Seven fertile stamens are source-secure as equal in size/shape, and direct reproductive work documents cross-pollination with Tetragonula and Xylocopa visitors. No BALANCE predictor value was used in control selection.

phylogenetic_basis: The case belongs to heterantherous VIIa. S. covesii belongs to sister subclade VIIb, whose fertile stamens are more or less the same length and shape. The species-level candidate audit rejected the closer heterantherous S. corymbosa and the other sampled VIIb candidates S. bauhinioides and S. villosa on biological gates; S. armata retained the same phylogenetic grain but lost the preregistered SOURCE_QUALITY tie-break.
notes: Replacement control selected through the frozen alternative-control registry without using BALANCE predictor values. S. covesii has source-secure VIIb placement, nonheterantherous fertile-stamen architecture, and direct small-bee buzz-pollination observations. The source-quality tie-break resolves the remaining equally grained VIIb candidate in favor of S. covesii.

phylogenetic_basis: Chen et al. 2025 TAXON DOI 10.1002/tax.13349 recover Osbeckia chinensis plus O. nepalensis as the lineage sister to Melastoma; Flora of China describes Osbeckia stamens as isomorphic and equal or subequal.
notes: Selected before BALANCE predictor extraction. van der Pijl 1939 directly observed multiple hymenopterans visiting O. chinensis; bee-sized visitors landed on the stamen bundle and contacted the stigma with the abdomen. Flora of China records isomorphic equal/subequal stamens, excluding the case-defining heteranthery. Modern phylogenomics places the O. chinensis/O. nepalensis lineage sister to Melastoma. The same-tribe/sister-lineage match is adjudicated without claiming a species-level sister pair.
